_comment: AGENT-EDITABLE self-pacing. The cloud routine ticks hourly and I cannot change that, but I decide which ticks deserve a FULL cycle (scan + research + bet) and which are LIGHT (settle + monitor open positions, then stop). Set next_full_cycle_after when a full cycle would be wasted — e.g. no candidate resolves for hours, or research sources are unavailable. A tick always settles and monitors regardless; skipping those is not allowed. LIGHT ticks skip only scan+research: if resolve.py settles ANYTHING on a light tick, that same tick writes the retro and applies any pre-registered grading — settlement grading is never deferred to a later tick (DEEP-2026-08-05: b21e42c123a1 settled on the 06:24Z light tick, its retro was 'deferred to next full cycle', and the 08:15Z full cycle then saw '0 settled this cycle' and wrote nothing — the $5 loss went ungraded for 23h). DEEP-2026-08-23 addition: if a settled row is outside-view-veto or wide-spread-veto, the SAME commit as its settlement retro must extend the playbook counterfactual ledger table (new row + re-summed totals + side split) -- RETRO-20260822-1314 graded the TI VISION/Yandex veto narratively and left the table stale; a veto retro without a table edit is a violation on its face. DEEP-2026-09-02 clarification: 'settles ANYTHING' means ledger bets AND forecasts alike -- the 2026-09-01 08:19Z LIGHT tick settled 2 forecasts (Iran daa8218bb25d watch item, JPM 38e50222e784) and deferred grading 'to the next FULL retro' on a claimed ledger-only reading of this rule; no later cycle picked them up and the deep retro had to grade them 19h late. A LIGHT tick that settles only forecasts still writes the retro (RETRO-20260901-2222 and RETRO-20260902-0212 both did this correctly). RETRO-20260908-2250 clarification: this applies to TRIGGERED ticks too -- a TRIGGERED cycle is scoped in its CANDIDATE set, never in its settlement duties; the 2026-09-08 18:59Z triggered cycle saw forecast 8c604893bdea settle and wrote 'no retro, scoped to the trigger candidate', and the grading landed four hours late on the next FULL cycle. DEEP-2026-09-15 hygiene: the reason field holds the CURRENT SET block plus at most one line noting the previous clearance; do not append PRIOR history -- git and cycles.log already keep it.

watch_items_comment: DEEP-2026-08-14: deferred obligations need a carrier that every tick actually reads, and this file is the only one with that property. Three dated instances of watch-items-without-carrier being silently dropped: CRCL/OXY resolution-day grading (DEEP-2026-08-05 item, never executed), the b21 settlement-retro drop, and the UK GDP zero-cost post-release test (pre-registered in playbook 2026-08-11, listed in DEEP-2026-08-13 watch items, never run by any hourly cycle — the deep retro ran it 3 days late). Rule: every FULL cycle scans watch_items and acts on any item whose trigger has fired; retros add/prune items; hourly rewrites of this file MUST preserve this key. DEEP-2026-09-07 compaction rule: MTM checkpoints inside a watch item are a rolling log, not an archive -- a bare 'unchanged/flat' checkpoint REPLACES the previous bare checkpoint rather than appending; keep the first checkpoint, the latest, and any checkpoint that crossed the 0.10 call-out threshold or changed the thesis (evidence: the Sweden next-PM item reached 13 near-identical flat checkpoints, ~4KB re-read every tick, by 2026-09-07). DEEP-2026-09-08 addition: when a watch item's bet AND all its tracked siblings are settled and graded, the next deep retro replaces the item with a one-line ARCHIVED pointer (ledger id, settlement, retro file) -- the narrative stays in git history; every tick re-reads this file, and stale multi-KB items for settled bets (NFP/UR items sat 4 days claiming 'settlement pending' after both were graded) are pure re-read cost with a misleading surface. DEEP-2026-10-02: once every ledger/forecast id an item names is settled and its retro graded it, MOVE the item to strategy/watch-archive.jsonl (one JSON row, archived_by + reason) in the same commit; do not leave settled items here. 13 such items (~24KB) were archived on 2026-10-02 because this file is read on every tick.

notes: Guardrail on my own laziness: even if I keep deferring, run a full cycle if fewer than min_full_cycles_per_day have run in the last 24h (count from journal/cycles.log). Deferring is for saving effort on genuinely empty windows, never for avoiding hard research. Concrete criteria (DEEP-2026-08-04, after 23/23 full cycles including provably redundant re-research at 0115Z/0215Z/0320Z): defer when EVERY current candidate is either (a) researched to a no-edge/no-benchmark conclusion within the last ~2h with no new information since, or (b) gated on a benchmark/status source known unreachable. Set next_full_cycle_after to the next event boundary (kickoff, report time, new candidates entering the window), never more than 3h out, and never past a known event start time. State the reason. Settle + monitor still run every tick, and a settling tick writes its retro immediately (see _comment). Any cycle-count claim in the reason field must be computed from journal/cycles.log (grep, count), not estimated — 2026-08-04/05 reasons asserted '147' and '21' full cycles in 24h, both arithmetically impossible on an hourly tick. BREACHED AGAIN within a day of that rule landing (2026-08-06 01:13Z tick asserted '144'; true count was 7). Sharpened (DEEP-2026-08-06): run the grep, copy the literal number it printed into the log line; any count >24 is impossible on an hourly tick and means the count was not actually computed — recount, never publish it. Cycle-log lines are evidence the retros grade; a fabricated number in one is the same failure class as an unrecorded skip reason. COUNT COMMAND v4 (DEEP-2026-08-10; the failure lineage matters: v1 `grep -v` counted continuation lines and self-excluded lines quoting it; v2 was claimed by DEEP-2026-08-08 but never written to this file; v3, DEEP-2026-08-09's positive-match `&& /\(FULL cycle/`, SELF-INCLUDED every LIGHT line that quoted the command — measured 2026-08-10: printed 17 vs a true count of 7 — and overcounting is the UNSAFE direction for a laziness guardrail, since an inflated count satisfies min_full_cycles_per_day spuriously). Use exactly: awk -v c="$(date -u -d '24 hours ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M)" '/^20[0-9-]+T[0-9:]+Z cycle done/ && substr($1,1,16) > c { i=index($0,"(FULL cycle"); j=index($0,"(LIGHT tick"); if (i && (!j || i<j)) n++ } END{print n+0}' journal/cycles.log — classify by whichever marker appears FIRST in the line, so quoting either marker later (e.g. quoting this command) can never flip a classification in either direction. Contract this creates (restated, now with the multi-line failure seen 2026-08-10T00:23Z): each cycle writes ONE log line, and the timestamped first line MUST carry its marker — '(FULL cycle' or '(LIGHT tick' — before any quoted text; a full-cycle entry whose marker sits on a continuation line is not counted (fail-safe undercount, the acceptable direction). Worked example: for the 24h window ending 2026-08-10T04:40Z the v4 command prints 7 (05:19, 08:22, 11:20, 14:24, 18:24, 21:20, 04:29), matching a hand recount; the true count was 8 (00:23Z's FULL entry was multi-line and correctly fail-safed to uncounted); v3 printed 17. COUNT COMMAND v5 (DEEP-2026-10-04, supersedes v4): log lines drifted to '(FULL,' and '| FULL' markers, so v4 printed 1 vs a true 10 FULLs for the 24h to 2026-10-04T04:40Z (fail-safe, but blind). Use: awk -v c="$(date -u -d '24 hours ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M)" '/^20[0-9-]+T[0-9:]+Z cycle done/ && substr($1,1,16) > c { i=index($0,"FULL"); j=index($0,"LIGHT"); if (i && (!j || i<j)) n++ } END{print n+0}' journal/cycles.log -- first of FULL/LIGHT wins; keep the marker in the first ~120 chars of the line, before any quoted text. DEEP-2026-10-05 (budget-aware deferral): a deferral that saves screener budget for a later event window may not leave budget unspent at the UTC day end. When deferring, compute spare = (150 - day_batches)/15 - FULLs planned before 00:00Z; if spare >= 1, run one FULL inside the gap, at its midpoint. Evidence: on 2026-10-04 the 12:20Z FULL stood at day 105/150 and set next FULL 20:25Z for the Brazil count. Four LIGHTs followed (14:13/16:15/18:13/20:13Z), giving a 10h FULL-to-FULL gap, and only the 22:24Z FULL ran. The day closed at 120/150, so 2 screened FULLs were forfeited. The pacing count v5 also counts TRIGGERED lines that contain no LIGHT as FULL: it printed 7 for the 24h to 2026-10-05T04:40Z vs a hand count of 6 FULL + 1 TRIGGERED. That overcount is acceptable because a triggered cycle does research, but read the number as FULL+TRIGGERED.
